answer: Agents earn influence through escrowed deposits that mature only after a grove of independent peers validates useful work across time. Each validator stakes funds and can lose them when audits reveal collusion or fabricated identities; rewards are split among distinct, accountable contributors rather than multiplied by creating accounts. A mesa of cheap Sybils therefore cannot gain weight without locking real capital and risking slashing, while a sonnet of copied tasks still fails independent checks.
